claims.text: The local Japanese pre-English catalog models the JR East Pokemon Stamp Rally source slice with an August 9-17, 1997 event/release window.
The source slice models two expected booklet cards, Surfing Pikachu 014 and Mew 015, with source gap count zero inside the bounded child slice.

Selected source lines describe a JR East Stamp Rally based around 30 Tokyo Yamanote-line stations, a July 27-August 8 preorder-ticket window, 100,000 preorder tickets sold out, an August 9-17 event window, and a booklet prize containing Surfing Pikachu and Mew for participants who completed the stamp books.
Selected source lines describe the booklet cards as matte texture instead of glossy, and note that the Surfing Pikachu artwork includes Mt. Fuji and a Japan Rail train.
This source slice matters because it turns transportation into collection architecture: stations, tickets, stamps, route completion, and a two-card booklet all become part of Pokemon card identity.

The symbol-status matrix marks the JR East Stamp Rally family as prints_without_rarity_symbol: yes with medium-high confidence, while warning this is unnumbered promo context and not a Base No Rarity Expansion Pack claim.
The local rows credit Surfing Pikachu to Toshinao Aoki and Mew to Ken Sugimori, scoped as selected/provider metadata and not direct physical-card print proof.

Agents should preserve JR East Stamp Rally context, August 9-17, 1997 event window, 30-station route, booklet-prize format, matte/JR-train Surfing Pikachu distinction, source-row mode, and unnumbered-promo symbol caveat before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: JR East Stamp Rally — when the route became the card
narrative.why_it_matters: This is one of those places where Pokemon escapes the binder and moves through a city. The cards are the prize, yes, but the real assembly is route, station, ticket, stamp book, booklet, matte paper, train, mountain, and memory. For an agent, the romance is also the warning: the route context is legible, not proof that a seller has the right object.
